chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A reliable explanatory method should fit the available facts while excluding comparably compatible rival explanations.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of the opening it answers, the stated requirement that explanations fit facts and discriminate among rivals supplies a positive standard for good evidence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Belief in God is not warranted by default; the believer must provide a good argument and supporting evidence.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently allocates the affirmative evidential burden and denies that belief becomes warranted merely because God has not been disproved.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The domino argument relies on an unsupported infinite-past model, while known time and causality are features of this universe.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without an earlier retained opposing move, the limits of known time and causality provide a standalone reason to withhold the argument's extrapolation beyond the universe.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Claims that God exists outside time and in every possible world remain unproved without a stated premise-and-conclusion argument.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a constructive burden test, the proposition requires support for the temporal and modal claims needed to connect a first cause to a necessarily existing God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Calling God axiomatic supplies neither an argument nor evidence, because assuming a claim where demonstration is unavailable does not establish its truth.

orphanFallback.rationale: The distinction between assumption and demonstration stands independently as a direct reason that axiomatic acceptance cannot itself constitute evidence for God.

chunk-003:c003-04.proposition: A claim that miracles occur is inadequate unless a particular miracle can be identified and reasonably attributed to a god.

orphanFallback.rationale: The demand for an identifiable event and a warranted divine attribution independently states the evidential conditions any miracle claim must satisfy.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: Axiomatic acceptance cannot establish God because incompatible gods or non-gods can be adopted in the same way, leaving no evidential means to distinguish them.

orphanFallback.rationale: The symmetry among incompatible axiomatic starting points is a standalone objection showing that the method lacks the discriminatory power required of evidence.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-02.proposition: Near-death and other extraordinary experiences are better treated as fallible, culturally shaped interpretations than as independently verified evidence for gods.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cultural variation, interpretive fallibility, and absent independent verification together provide a constructive basis for declining to infer divine causation from extraordinary reports.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-10.proposition: Competing beliefs should be tested under shared and consistently applied evidential standards rather than granting God a special axiomatic exemption.

orphanFallback.rationale: Comparing worldviews by common standards, consistency, and parsimony independently supplies a method for detecting special pleading in theistic evidence.

chunk-006:c006-10.proposition: Treating resurrection as literal while classifying commands concerning killing or slavery as hyperbole requires a non-selective basis for distinguishing literal from figurative scripture.

orphanFallback.rationale: The contrast among resurrection, conquest, and slavery passages independently raises a consistency test for any method used to classify scriptural claims as literal or hyperbolic.
